name: Anneal-Caldera
geological_features: Active supervolcanoes along the equatorial ridge
Lava tube networks spanning hundreds of kilometers
Tectonic rift valleys glowing with exposed magma
specific_features: Abandoned mining complex on a cooled lava plateau
Exotic matter deposits in the deepest lava tubes
description: Anneal-Caldera is a world perpetually remaking itself, its surface a tortured landscape of active calderas, flowing lava rivers, and cooling basalt plains that crack and reform in endless cycles. The equatorial ridge hosts a chain of supervolcanoes whose eruptions paint the toxic sky in shades of crimson and ochre, while rivers of molten rock carve new channels through terrain that is never the same twice. The air shimmers with heat distortion, making the horizon ripple like a living thing.

The atmosphere is a choking mix of sulfur dioxide, carbon monoxide, and volcanic ash that would kill an unprotected human in minutes. The ground trembles with constant seismic activity, a low vibration that becomes so ubiquitous visitors in shielded habitats forget it is there until it stops, which is when they should be most afraid. The sound of the planet is a deep, continuous roar overlaid with the sharp crack of cooling rock and the hiss of superheated gases escaping through vents.

Extremophile microbes thrive in the lava tube networks, metabolizing sulfur compounds and trace metals in conditions that mirror theoretical models of early planetary biogenesis. A mining operation established on a cooled plateau extracted high-grade titanium for decades before a caldera breach made the site untenable; the abandoned equipment has since been partially consumed by fresh lava flows. Deep within the most ancient lava tubes, deposits of exotic matter suggest the planet's volcanic activity may be driven by something more unusual than simple geological processes.

The exotic matter deposits represent Anneal-Caldera's greatest prize and greatest danger, requiring deep penetration into an actively volcanic world to access. Three separate extraction attempts have ended in catastrophe, earning the planet a reputation that makes recruiting crews difficult. Yet the deposits are among the purest known, and the consortium that successfully develops a viable extraction method stands to reshape the sector's economy.
